article.headline: Snowflake Grows Sales 35% As Its Losses Narrow
article.deck: Snowflake bounced off its 50-day line inside a seven-week cup; the buy point is 384.66, 13.3% above the close, with an earlier entry at the 348.38 handle high.
body: Snowflake sells a data platform that runs in the cloud. Companies load their data into it to keep a single record, run analysis, build applications on top of it and share data with partners. The company now pitches it as an AI Data Cloud, which applies AI models to that data. Its customers span finance, advertising, media, retail, health care, manufacturing, telecom and travel.

The growth is in sales. Revenue for the July quarter rose 35.1% from a year earlier to 1.55 billion. The four quarters given show steady sequential gains: 1.21 billion, 1.28 billion, 1.39 billion and 1.55 billion. The company still loses money, but the loss narrowed: 0.87 a share, then 0.90, 0.86 and 0.55 in the latest quarter.

The market pays up for that growth. Snowflake carries a market value of 117.76 billion and trades at 110.5 times forward earnings. The stock is up 52.1% this year and 31.9% over 12 months, though it has slipped 0.7% over the past month.

On Monday the stock rose 8.20, or 2.5%, to 333.63. The day's low touched the 50-day line, at 331.76, and the stock closed above it. Volume was 0.29x the 50-day average. It sits 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line, right on it.

The chart is a seven-week cup, 21.4% deep, with its high on Sept. 3 and its low on Oct. 16. The buy point is 384.66 and the buy range runs to 403.89. The close is 13.3% below the buy point and 13.2% under the 52-week high of 384.56. Two earlier entries show on the chart: the handle's high from Sept. 30 at 348.38, 4.2% above the close, and the bounce entry above the day's high of 338.09, with the 50-day line as the stop.

Relative strength is the standout. Snowflake holds RS rank 92 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 7.9% off its high while the price is 13.2% off its own. The stock trades 40.9% above its 200-day line.
The week's headlines were commentary rather than company news: one weighed Wall Street's bullish views, another asked how low the stock can go. The next earnings report is due Dec. 2.

article.headline: Zeta Global Holds Gains After Goldman Sees 41% Upside
article.deck: Zeta is 2.3% above the 32.91 buy point of a four-week flat base, inside a buy range that ends at 34.56.
body: Zeta Global eased 0.31, or 0.9%, to 33.67. The stock cleared a four-week flat base with a 32.91 buy point on Oct. 5 and sits 2.3% above it, inside the buy range that runs to 34.56. The base was 14.6% deep, with its high on Sept. 4 and its low on Sept. 28. Volume was 0.21x the 50-day average; the breakout session traded 1.17x.

Fifteen sessions after the breakout, the stock is 5.8% under its 52-week high of 35.75. It trades 8.1% above its 50-day line and 50.9% above its 200-day line, and 0.31 ATRs from the 21-day line, close to the line. It holds RS rank 94 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 1.6% under its high. The stock is up 65.5% this year and 80.1% over 12 months.

The June quarter showed EPS of 0.03 on revenue of 442.8 million, up 43.5% from a year earlier. Revenue climbed in each of the four quarters given, from 337.2 million to 442.8 million, while EPS swung between small losses and small profits. The stock trades at 28.0 times forward earnings. The next report is due Nov. 3.

A headline last week said Goldman sees 41% upside in the stock. Earlier in October, headlines said Zeta unveiled AthenaOS to connect AI, data and marketing workflows and expanded with a Digital Audience buyout.
A close under 32.91 would stall the move.
article.watch: The 32.91 buy point into the Nov. 3 earnings report.

market_note: The S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7674.79 and the Nasdaq gained 0.9% to 26190.05, but both closed under their 50-day lines, the S&P 500 by 0.3% and the Nasdaq by 1.5%. The Dow added 0.2% to 52320.14 and sits 0.1% above its 50-day line. The S&P 500 carries 5 distribution days over the last 25 sessions, the Dow 4 and the Nasdaq 3, and the desk's state stays Market in correction. Leadership is narrow but not empty: LNG, NOW, BRK-B and TSLA moved past buy points this week, software leads the groups with an average RS of 72 and 80% of its names above the 50-day line, energy follows at 68, and only 17% of the AI chip group holds its 50-day line.

chief.verdict: The leadership is narrow and the breakouts are thin: LNG cleared 300.99 today on 0.49 times average volume, TSLA cleared 386.93 on 0.86, and NOW and XOM sit near the top of their buy ranges with earnings two and four days out. The cleanest charts are in software, the one group with real breadth (average RS 72, 80% of names above the 50-day), while ai chips have only 17% above the 50-day and fintech 5%. With the S&P 500 0.3% below its 50-day and the Nasdaq 1.5% below its 50-day, the risk is on the downside, and new buys should be small and limited to the strongest charts.
chief.market: Market in correction with 5 S&P 500 distribution days and 3 on the Nasdaq in 25 sessions: hold mostly cash, take only a starter position or two, and wait for a follow-through day before adding exposure.

picks.why: It has the best relative strength on the desk at RS 96, and its RS line is only 1.8% off its high while the stock is 3.0% below its 52-week high. It is still 0.9% above the 55.65 buy point and today's -0.2% dip came on 0.36 times average volume, which is a quiet hold, not selling. The risks are the 5-week cup (short for a cup, 20.4% deep), a 2026-10-12 breakout on just 0.87 times volume, and a -0.22 loss per share in the latest quarter.
picks.entry: Buy within the 55.65 to 58.43 buy range, and only on a day that closes higher on above-average volume; a close back below 55.65 cancels the trade.

picks.why: RS 92 with revenue up 35.1%, and today's low touched the 50-day line (331.76) before the stock closed 2.5% higher at 333.63. That makes the risk very small, which is the only kind of risk worth taking in a correction. The risks are that the bounce came on 0.29 times average volume, the cup is 21.4% deep and 13.3% below its 384.66 buy point, and the company still loses money (-0.55 a share).
picks.entry: Start a half position above today's high at 338.09 with a stop on a close below the 50-day line at 331.76; add above the 348.38 handle high, and add the rest only through 384.66.

picks.why: RS 94 with an RS line 1.6% off its high, a 14.6% flat base that broke out 2026-10-05 on 1.17 times volume, and revenue up 43.5%. Today's -0.9% came on 0.21 times average volume, so nobody is selling. Earnings land 2026-11-03, and a new position bought at 33.67, 2.3% above the 32.91 buy point, would carry the full earnings risk.
picks.entry: Wait for the 2026-11-03 report; buy a gap or close above the 35.75 52-week high on heavy volume, or a pullback that holds the 32.91 buy point.

picks.why: A tidy 12-week flat base only 9.7% deep, a 50-day bounce today (low touched 316.94, close 320.09), and EPS up 36.4%. But earnings come 2026-10-28, two sessions away, and RS 68 is not leadership.
picks.entry: No buy before the 2026-10-28 report; after it, the early entry is a move above the 324.06 handle high and the standard buy point is 336.04, with buy range up to 352.84.

avoid.why: The 300.99 cup breakout came on 0.49 times average volume, the RS line is 15.8% below its high, and earnings on 2026-10-29 come in three sessions, so this is a breakout without buyers right in front of a report.
It fell 2.1% today, sits 12.7% above its 50-day at 155.67, close to the 157.19 top of the buy range, while EPS fell 21.6% and earnings on 2026-10-28 come in two sessions.
The 6.1% jump through 386.93 came on 0.86 times volume and analyst merger talk, with RS 62, an RS line 28.6% off its high, EPS down 43.6%, and the stock 20.8% below its 52-week high.
A 28.3% deep, loose cup 50.8% below its 52-week high with an RS line 55.0% off its high: it is a bounce in a long downtrend, sitting 15.0% above its 50-day, not a leader breaking out.

chief.watch: Watch whether the Nasdaq, at 26,190.05 and 1.5% below its 50-day, can close back above that line on higher volume; a sixth S&P distribution day would mean no new buys at all.
